claims.text: Premelting and melting behavior in Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles is governed by local lattice strain induced by nanoscale compositional heterogeneity.
Nanoscale compositional heterogeneity creates regions with reduced local melting points.
Regions with reduced local melting points initiate surface premelting at lower temperatures than in a more chemically homogeneous structure.
The nanoparticles are initially solid and equimolar in Fe, Ni, Cr, Co, and Cu.
Controlled thermal annealing reduces short-range chemical ordering in these nanoparticles.
Reducing short-range chemical ordering reduces atomic-scale compositional heterogeneity.
Atomic-scale compositional fluctuations generate regions of high lattice strain.
High lattice strain lowers the local free-energy barrier to atomic mobility.
The lower barrier to atomic mobility causes earlier surface premelting.
As-synthesized nanoparticles have greater chemical heterogeneity than the annealed nanoparticles.
As-synthesized nanoparticles will exhibit surface-premelting onset at a lower temperature than annealed nanoparticles.
As-synthesized nanoparticles will have a lower whole-particle melting temperature than annealed nanoparticles.
